To remove (markings or information).

examples.text: I erased that word from the page because it was wrong.

glosses: To obliterate information from (a storage medium), such as to clear or (with magnetic storage) to demagnetize.

examples.text: I'm going to erase this tape.

glosses: To obliterate (information) from a storage medium, such as to clear or to overwrite.

examples.text: I'm going to erase those files.

glosses: To remove a runner from the bases via a double play or pick off play

examples.text: Jones was erased by a 6-4-3 double play.

glosses: To be erased (have markings removed, have information removed, or be cleared of information).

examples.text: The chalkboard erased easily.
The files will erase quickly.

glosses: To disregard (a group, an orientation, etc.); to prevent from having an active role in society.

examples.text: I suggest, then, that counterdiscourses, when reductive, tend to emulate the screen discourse that erases gay sociality.
As a result, Palestinians are hyperpresent in Israeli media, while Mizrahim are erased from public discourse.

glosses: To kill; assassinate.
The operation of deleting data.

examples.text: This subsystem is waiting to become Exclusive after having issued an erase.

glosses: To delete or erase or remove (something) by rubbing, especially with a rubber (eraser).

examples.text: The teacher wanted to rub out the chalk marks on the blackboard.

glosses: To get by; to live.

examples.text: The first will understand but little of them, the latter over much; they might perhaps live and rub out in the middle region.

glosses: To kill, especially to murder.

examples.text: It was just a week to the day since Mr. Martin had decided to rub out Mrs. Ulgine Barrows.
